initial_reasons.AGNES: Enters guarded and ready to judge Will's return.
initial_reasons.WILL: Enters cautiously, hoping the new house can bridge the distance between them.

AGNES.reason: His practical question exposes the hurt behind his failure to show her the house himself.
Hearing Hamnet's death named in the house brings the loss fully into the exchange.
Her account of grief in every second and minute reveals that the loss remains continuously present.
She rejects the apology by identifying his attachment to the mental world that keeps him away from her.
Naming their child's death as something that could not interrupt his other life sharpens her accusation.
The charge that he should have been present becomes an unmistakable judgment of his absence.

WILL.reason: Her question immediately touches his guilt and makes him briefly avoid her eyes.
His admission about wondering where Hamnet is turns his attention inward toward an imagined search.
The apology is a direct attempt to acknowledge the shared wound.
Her description of a place in his head forces him to confront how she experiences his withdrawal.
Hearing the death of their child framed as evidence against him makes his guilt visible.
Her accusation lands on the farewell he was absent for and overwhelms his defensive posture.
